confucius-01.translation: Isn't it a joy to learn and return to what you have learned?
confucius-01.note: Learning becomes yours when you revisit it and put it into practice.

confucius-02.translation: Isn't it a delight when friends come from far away?
confucius-02.note: A friend who makes the journey to see you is a reason for joy.

confucius-03.translation: Revisit what you know, and discover something new.
confucius-03.note: Looking again at an old lesson can reveal a meaning you missed.

confucius-04.translation: Know what you know, and admit what you don't. That is understanding.
confucius-04.note: Honesty about the limits of your knowledge is part of wisdom.

confucius-05.translation: Among the people I walk with, someone always has something to teach me.
confucius-05.note: You can learn from the people around you, whatever their role or age.

confucius-06.translation: Do not do to others what you would not want done to you.
confucius-06.note: Before you act, imagine how it would feel to be on the receiving end.

confucius-07.translation: Worry less about being understood, and more about understanding others.
confucius-07.note: Turn your attention from getting recognition to noticing other people.

confucius-08.translation: A person of character is more than a tool for a single task.
confucius-08.note: Grow your judgment and character, rather than defining yourself by one useful skill.

confucius-09.translation: Each day, I examine myself in three ways.
confucius-09.note: In the Analects, Zengzi asks whether he has been faithful, trustworthy and practiced what he learned.

confucius-10.translation: Only in the cold do we see how long the pine and cypress keep their leaves.
confucius-10.note: Difficult times reveal the qualities that remain steady within a person.

confucius-11.translation: I guide those eager to understand, and help those struggling to express a thought.
confucius-11.note: A teacher can help most when a learner is already reaching for an answer.

confucius-12.translation: Good character does not stand alone; it draws others near.
confucius-12.note: Living with care and integrity can bring you people who value the same things.

confucius-13.translation: A person of character is at ease; a small-minded person is always troubled.
confucius-13.note: A wider concern for what is right can loosen the grip of everyday worries.

confucius-14.translation: To make a mistake and refuse to correct it is the real mistake.
confucius-14.note: What matters is not being perfect, but being willing to change.

confucius-15.translation: Firmness, resolve, simplicity and modest speech bring us close to kindness.
confucius-15.note: A caring character is built through steady actions, not polished words alone.

confucius-16.translation: Do not worry about having no position. Work on what makes you fit for one.
confucius-16.note: Focus on becoming ready for responsibility rather than chasing a title.

confucius-17.translation: Without thought for the future, trouble will soon come near.
confucius-17.note: Making a little room for tomorrow can prevent problems today.

confucius-18.translation: A person of character looks for what is right; a small-minded person looks for gain.
confucius-18.note: Ask whether a choice is fair before asking what you can get from it.

confucius-19.translation: When it comes to doing what is humane, do not hold back even for your teacher.
confucius-19.note: Respect does not mean waiting for someone else to do the caring thing first.

confucius-20.translation: Aim for the Way, stand on good character, rely on kindness, and explore the arts.
confucius-20.note: A full life joins a sense of direction, moral care and the pleasure of learning skills.

laozi-01.translation: A way put into words is not the lasting Way.
laozi-01.note: Words can point toward experience, but cannot contain all of it.

laozi-02.translation: Understanding others is wisdom; understanding yourself is clarity.
laozi-02.note: Looking inward matters just as much as being good at reading other people.

laozi-03.translation: The highest goodness is like water.
laozi-03.note: Water helps life without competing, and flows to places others avoid.

laozi-04.translation: A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath your feet.
laozi-04.note: A distant goal starts with the step you can take right now.

laozi-05.translation: Those who know when they have enough are rich.
laozi-05.note: Feeling wealthy can come from contentment, not just from owning more.

laozi-06.translation: The soft and yielding overcome the hard and strong.
laozi-06.note: Flexibility can outlast a force that knows only how to resist.

laozi-07.translation: The greatest skill can look awkward.
laozi-07.note: Deep skill need not show itself through decoration or display.

laozi-08.translation: Good fortune leans on trouble; trouble hides within good fortune.
laozi-08.note: What seems good or bad can change, so avoid judging a whole situation too quickly.

laozi-09.translation: Those who know do not talk; those who talk do not know.
laozi-09.note: The sharp contrast invites us to question whether words are replacing real understanding.

laozi-10.translation: Nothing in the world is softer or weaker than water.
laozi-10.note: The wider passage uses water to show how gentleness can wear down what is hard.

laozi-11.translation: Learning adds something each day; following the Way lets something go each day.
laozi-11.note: Gathering knowledge and letting go of needless effort are different kinds of growth.

laozi-12.translation: Act without forcing, and nothing is left undone.
laozi-12.note: This is not a call to do nothing, but to act without pushing against everything.

laozi-13.translation: A great vessel takes time to finish.
laozi-13.note: Important abilities may develop slowly. This follows the wording of the supplied text.

laozi-14.translation: Too many words soon run out. Better to keep your center.
laozi-14.note: Constant explaining can drain you; a steady inner balance may help more.

laozi-15.translation: To understand what endures is clarity.
laozi-15.note: Look for the steady patterns within a world that keeps changing.

laozi-16.translation: Those who overcome themselves are strong.
laozi-16.note: Working with your own habits can take more strength than defeating someone else.

laozi-17.translation: Take as much care at the end as you did at the beginning.
laozi-17.note: Keep paying attention when a task feels almost finished.

laozi-18.translation: A tree you can barely embrace grows from a tiny shoot.
laozi-18.note: Large things begin small. Give small beginnings the care they need.

laozi-19.translation: Finish the work without holding on to the credit.
laozi-19.note: You can do something well without making the achievement your whole identity.

laozi-20.translation: By not showing off, you become clear to others.
laozi-20.note: Let the quality of your actions speak instead of constantly drawing attention to yourself.

sunzi-01.translation: Know the other side and yourself, and a hundred battles need not put you in danger.
sunzi-01.note: Good judgment needs an honest view of both your situation and the other side's.

sunzi-02.translation: Bring the opposing army to yield without fighting.
sunzi-02.note: The surrounding passage values reaching an outcome without the destruction of battle.

sunzi-03.translation: Warfare is a way of deception.
sunzi-03.note: This describes military strategy. It is not advice to deceive people in everyday relationships.

sunzi-04.translation: Strike where they are unprepared; appear where they do not expect you.
sunzi-04.note: In a military setting, preparation includes noticing gaps in the other side's expectations.

sunzi-05.translation: In war, value victory rather than a long campaign.
sunzi-05.note: A conflict that drags on drains resources and harms the people involved.

sunzi-06.translation: A skilled commander draws others into position, rather than being drawn by them.
sunzi-06.note: Try to shape a situation thoughtfully instead of only reacting to pressure.

sunzi-07.translation: Know the weather and the ground, and victory can be complete.
sunzi-07.note: Understanding people is not enough; timing and surroundings also matter.

sunzi-08.translation: An army has no fixed pattern, just as water has no fixed shape.
sunzi-08.note: A good plan changes with the conditions rather than clinging to one form.

sunzi-09.translation: Move swiftly like the wind; move slowly with the stillness of a forest.
sunzi-09.note: Match your pace to the situation. Speed is useful only when it fits.

sunzi-10.translation: Knowledge in advance cannot be obtained from spirits.
sunzi-10.note: The passage calls for information from people, rather than guesses or supernatural signs.

sunzi-11.translation: Winning every battle is not the highest kind of skill.
sunzi-11.note: Avoiding the need for a fight can be better than repeatedly winning one.

sunzi-12.translation: The best strategy is to defeat the other side's plans.
sunzi-12.note: Sun Tzu places disrupting a strategy above meeting armies in battle.

sunzi-13.translation: War is a matter of great importance to a state.
sunzi-13.note: The opening treats war as a grave decision, not something to enter lightly.

sunzi-14.translation: Those who know when to fight and when not to fight will win.
sunzi-14.note: Choosing whether to enter a conflict comes before choosing how to fight it.

sunzi-15.translation: Place them where they could perish, and only then will they survive.
sunzi-15.note: This is a historical military claim about desperate situations, not advice to endanger yourself or others.

sunzi-16.translation: A skilled commander avoids an enemy whose spirit is sharp.
sunzi-16.note: Rather than meeting peak force head-on, consider when the situation will change.

sunzi-17.translation: Wait nearby for those who travel far; wait rested for those who are tired.
sunzi-17.note: Preparation and conserving energy can matter more than rushing into action.

sunzi-18.translation: Speed is central to the nature of warfare.
sunzi-18.note: In the military context of the passage, an opportunity can disappear if action comes too late.

sunzi-19.translation: A commander needs wisdom, trustworthiness, kindness, courage and discipline.
sunzi-19.note: Leadership is not only about force. Care for people and reliability matter too.

sunzi-20.translation: A winning army secures the conditions for victory before seeking battle.
sunzi-20.note: Build a sound position before committing yourself, rather than relying on hope afterward.

confucius-21.translation: Learning without thinking leaves you empty-handed; thinking without learning leaves you on thin ice.
confucius-21.note: Taking things in and testing them for yourself only work as a pair.

confucius-22.translation: Knowing something falls short of liking it, and liking it falls short of delighting in it.
confucius-22.note: The same work goes deeper depending on what draws you to it.

confucius-23.translation: A person of character is in harmony without becoming the same; a lesser one becomes the same without ever being in harmony.
confucius-23.note: Real agreement keeps differences; false agreement erases them and connects no one.

confucius-24.translation: Meet someone admirable and want to match them; meet someone who falls short and look inward.
confucius-24.note: Watching others becomes useful only when it turns into a look at yourself.

confucius-25.translation: A craftsman who wants to do the work well sharpens the tools first.
confucius-25.note: Good results come out of the time spent getting ready.

laozi-21.translation: Heaven's net is vast; its mesh is wide, and still nothing slips through.
laozi-21.note: What looks loose and slow is not the same as what never arrives.

laozi-22.translation: Words you can trust are not dressed up; dressed-up words are not ones to trust.
laozi-22.note: What is pleasant to hear and what is accurate often part ways.

laozi-23.translation: Know when you have enough and nothing shames you; know where to stop and nothing endangers you.
laozi-23.note: Knowing where to stop is its own kind of protection.

laozi-24.translation: Governing a large country is like cooking a small fish.
laozi-24.note: Turn it too often and it falls apart; restraint is part of the work.

laozi-25.translation: The heavy is the root of the light; the still governs the restless.
laozi-25.note: Whatever stays steady ends up setting the pace for whatever does not.

sunzi-21.translation: In battle you meet the other side head-on and win by the unexpected.
sunzi-21.note: A surprise only works once the straightforward part is solid.

sunzi-22.translation: Those who fight well look to the situation for an answer instead of blaming the people.
sunzi-22.note: Blaming people for a bad outcome leaves whatever caused it untouched.

sunzi-23.translation: Do not count on the other side staying away; count on being ready for them.
sunzi-23.note: Preparation rests on what you have done, not on what you hope they will not do.

sunzi-24.translation: Those who defend well hide as if nine layers underground.
sunzi-24.note: Defence starts with not showing what you have.

sunzi-25.translation: The side that wins the reckoning before the fight is the side that counted more.
sunzi-25.note: Much of the outcome is settled by how thoroughly you worked it out beforehand.

confucius-01-01.translation: Learn, and keep taking it up again in season — is that not a pleasure? Friends come from far away — is that not a joy? People fail to recognize you and it does not sour you — is that not the mark of character?
confucius-01-01.note: Three things in one breath. The first two are pleasures; the third says the pleasure does not depend on anyone noticing.

confucius-01-02a.translation: Someone who serves parents and elders well is rarely one who likes defying those above; and no one who dislikes defying them has ever liked starting a revolt. A person of character works at the root, and once the root stands, a way opens.
confucius-01-02a.note: How you behave close to home turns up again far from it.

confucius-01-02b.translation: Serving parents and elders — is that not the root of humaneness?
confucius-01-02b.note: The conclusion of the passage before it: the largest virtue starts in the closest relationship.

confucius-01-03.translation: Polished words and a managed expression — humaneness is rare in them.
confucius-01-03.note: A surface arranged to please does not stand in for what is underneath.

confucius-01-04.translation: Each day I check myself on three counts. Planning for others, did I hold anything back? Dealing with friends, was I someone they could rely on? What I was taught, did I practise it?
confucius-01-04.note: The items are fixed at three. That is what separates this from vague self-reproach.

confucius-01-05.translation: To lead a state of a thousand chariots: treat the work with care and be reliable, spend sparingly and spare the people, call them to service only in season.
confucius-01-05.note: Governing written as three practical habits rather than an ideal.

confucius-01-06.translation: At home, serve your parents; outside, defer to your elders; be careful and reliable; care for people widely and stay close to those who are humane. If strength is left over after that, then study texts.
confucius-01-06.note: Book learning comes last here, and the order is the point.

confucius-01-07.translation: Honour the worthy rather than be swayed by appearances; serve your parents with all your strength; serve your ruler with your whole self; keep your word with friends. Even if such a person never studied, I would call them learned.
confucius-01-07.note: Learning measured by conduct instead of by texts read.

confucius-01-08.translation: Without weight a person commands no respect; with learning they do not harden. Put loyalty and reliability at the centre, do not take as friends those you cannot learn from, and when you are wrong do not shrink from changing.
confucius-01-08.note: The last clause carries the rest: not shrinking from the correction.

confucius-01-09.translation: Treat endings with care and keep the distant dead in mind, and the character of a people grows thicker.
confucius-01-09.note: How a community handles endings changes its grain.

confucius-01-10a.translation: Ziqin asked Zigong: wherever the Master goes, he always hears how that state is run — does he ask for it, or is he told? Zigong said: he is warm, good, respectful, sparing and yielding, and that is how it comes to him.
confucius-01-10a.note: Some doors open without being asked. The manner had arrived first.

confucius-01-10b.translation: If the Master does seek it, surely he seeks it unlike the way others do?
confucius-01-10b.note: The same thing can be arrived at by a different road.

confucius-01-11.translation: While the father lives, watch the son's intent; once he is gone, watch his conduct. If for three years he does not turn from his father's way, that may be called filial.
confucius-01-11.note: Where you stand to judge someone shifts with the occasion.

confucius-01-12.translation: In the use of ritual, harmony is what is precious; this is what made the old kings' way fine, and matters large and small follow it. Yet something fails here: to know only harmony and chase it, without ritual to shape and limit it, does not work either.
confucius-01-12.note: Harmony is held precious and, in the same breath, declared not enough on its own.

confucius-01-13.translation: When reliability stays near what is right, a promise can be kept; when respect stays near ritual, disgrace keeps its distance. To lean on others and still not lose those closest to you is also worth honouring.
confucius-01-13.note: Even a good quality needs something to rest against before it does its work.

confucius-01-14.translation: A person of character does not eat for fullness or live for comfort, is quick in work and careful in speech, and goes to those who have the way to be set straight. That is what loving learning means.
confucius-01-14.note: "Loves learning" spelled out as conditions of daily life.

confucius-01-15a.translation: Zigong asked: poor without flattering, well-off without arrogance — how is that? The Master said: acceptable. But short of being poor and glad, well-off and fond of ritual.
confucius-01-15a.note: Not doing the wrong thing ranks below actually delighting in the right one.

confucius-01-15b.translation: Zigong said: the Odes speak of cutting and filing, carving and polishing — is this what that means? The Master said: Si, now I can talk about the Odes with you. Tell you what has gone and you see what is coming.
confucius-01-15b.note: The moment learning catches. Told one thing, he sees the thing not told.

confucius-01-16.translation: Do not fret that others fail to know you; fret that you fail to know them.
confucius-01-16.note: It turns the worry around to face the other way.

confucius-02-01.translation: Govern by character and you are the north star: it stays where it is, and the other stars turn around it.
confucius-02-01.note: The pull does not come from moving about. It comes from holding a position.

confucius-02-02.translation: Three hundred poems, and one line covers them all: nothing crooked in the thinking.
confucius-02-02.note: Pulling a whole body of work into a single line is itself a way of reading.

confucius-02-03.translation: Lead with regulations and level them with punishment: people dodge it and feel no shame. Lead with character and level them with ritual: they feel shame and straighten themselves.
confucius-02-03.note: Punishment stops the act. Shame changes what the person wants.

confucius-02-04.translation: At fifteen I set my mind on learning; at thirty I stood; at forty I stopped wavering; at fifty I knew what heaven had given me; at sixty my ear went along with what it heard; at seventy I could follow what my heart wanted and still not cross the line.
confucius-02-04.note: A life marked off in decades. In the last one, what he wanted and what was allowed turn out to be the same.

confucius-02-05a.translation: Meng Yizi asked about filial conduct. The Master said: do not go against it. Later, with Fan Chi driving, the Master said: Mengsun asked me about filial conduct and I told him not to go against it. Fan Chi said: what does that mean?
confucius-02-05a.note: A short answer, then raised again elsewhere. Making someone ask back is part of the teaching.

confucius-02-05b.translation: While they live, serve them by the rites; when they die, bury them by the rites and offer to them by the rites.
confucius-02-05b.note: The answer held back earlier lands here: this is what not going against it meant.

confucius-02-06.translation: Meng Wubo asked about filial conduct. The Master said: your parents worry about one thing only, that you fall ill.
confucius-02-06.note: Instead of listing a child's duties, he turns it around to what the parents feel.

confucius-02-07.translation: Ziyou asked about filial conduct. The Master said: these days it means being able to provide. But dogs and horses get provided for too. Without respect, what sets the two apart?
confucius-02-07.note: Supplying someone and treating them as a person, set side by side so the gap shows.

confucius-02-08.translation: Zixia asked about filial conduct. The Master said: the look on your face is the hard part. When there is work, the young take the labour; when there is food and drink, the elders are served. Is that alone filial?
confucius-02-08.note: The tasks can be imitated. What shows on your face cannot.

confucius-02-09.translation: I talk with Hui all day and he never pushes back, as if he were slow. But look at what he does once he leaves, and it is all there. Hui is not slow.
confucius-02-09.note: Saying little is not the same as missing the point. It shows in what he does afterwards.

confucius-02-10.translation: Look at what someone does, trace how they got there, see what puts them at ease. Where could a person hide? Where could they hide?
confucius-02-10.note: Three layers: the act, the route, and what makes them comfortable. A performance does not survive all three.

confucius-02-11.translation: Warm up the old and find what is new in it, and you can be someone others learn from.
confucius-02-11.note: Storing something away and bringing it back to life are two different acts.

confucius-02-12.translation: A person of character is not a vessel.
confucius-02-12.note: Not a tool with one fixed use.

confucius-02-13.translation: Zigong asked about the person of character. The Master said: act on it first, and let your words come after.
confucius-02-13.note: Reverse the order and the words turn into a debt.

confucius-02-14.translation: A person of character is wide in their dealings and forms no faction; a lesser one forms factions and is never wide.
confucius-02-14.note: Being open to many and closing into a circle pull in opposite directions.

confucius-02-15.translation: Learn without thinking and nothing stays; think without learning and you are on thin ice.
confucius-02-15.note: Taking in and testing: neither stands on its own.

confucius-02-16.translation: To go hard at what lies at one extreme does harm, and nothing else.
confucius-02-16.note: Fixing on one far end becomes its own trouble. Readers have long disagreed about this line.

confucius-02-17.translation: You, shall I tell you what knowing is? To treat what you know as known and what you do not as unknown — that is knowing.
confucius-02-17.note: Knowledge starts by drawing the edge of what you know.

confucius-02-18.translation: Zizhang wanted to learn how to secure a salary. The Master said: hear much, set aside what is doubtful, speak the rest with care, and there is little to blame. See much, set aside what is risky, act on the rest with care, and there is little to regret. Few blames in speech and few regrets in action, and the salary is already in there.
confucius-02-18.note: Asked how to get a post, he answers with how to become someone a post comes to.

confucius-02-19.translation: Duke Ai asked: what makes the people fall in behind you? Confucius answered: raise the straight and set them above the crooked, and they will; raise the crooked and set them above the straight, and they will not.
confucius-02-19.note: People do not watch the slogans. They watch who gets promoted.

confucius-02-20.translation: Ji Kangzi asked: how do I get the people to be respectful, loyal, and willing to urge each other on? The Master said: meet them with weight and they are respectful; serve your parents and care for those under you and they are loyal; raise the capable and teach those who are not, and they urge each other on.
confucius-02-20.note: For each thing demanded, he names who has to move first, and hands it back.

confucius-02-21.translation: Someone said to Confucius: why do you not take office? He said: the Documents say, be filial, be good to your brothers. Carry that into public affairs and it is already governing. Why should governing have to mean holding a post?
confucius-02-21.note: He lifts governing out of officialdom and sets it back down in the household.

confucius-02-22.translation: If a person has nothing others can rely on, I do not know what can be made of them. A large cart without its yoke-pin, a small one without its collar-bar — how would either move?
confucius-02-22.note: The part that looks minor is the one the whole cart waits on.

confucius-02-23.translation: Zizhang asked: can we know ten dynasties ahead? The Master said: Yin carried on the rites of Xia, and what was dropped and added can be known; Zhou carried on the rites of Yin, and what was dropped and added can be known. Whoever carries on from Zhou — even a hundred dynasties ahead could be known.
confucius-02-23.note: Once you see how each one inherits and adjusts, the far future stops being blank.

confucius-02-24.translation: To offer sacrifice to spirits not your own is flattery. To see what is right and not do it is cowardice.
confucius-02-24.note: What you should not do and what you should, set down side by side.

confucius-03-01.translation: Of the Ji family he said: eight rows of dancers in their courtyard. If this can be borne, what cannot?
confucius-03-01.note: A rank took the ceremony of a rank far above it. Cross one line and the next gets easier.

confucius-03-02.translation: The three families cleared the altar to the Yong hymn. The Master said: it sings of princes assisting and the Son of Heaven in solemn state. What use is that in the halls of three families?
confucius-03-02.note: When the words and the setting do not match, ceremony turns into decoration.

confucius-03-03.translation: If a person is not humane, what has ritual to do with them? If a person is not humane, what has music to do with them?
confucius-03-03.note: A form is only a form when there is something to put inside it.

confucius-03-04.translation: Lin Fang asked what lies at the root of ritual. The Master said: a large question. In ritual, better plain than lavish; in mourning, better grieved than smoothly done.
confucius-03-04.note: When the outward form and the feeling pull apart, he says take the feeling.

confucius-03-05.translation: That the border peoples have rulers is not like the Xia states having none.
confucius-03-05.note: Readers split on this one. Flipped around, it says even the borderlands keep order while the central states have lost it.

confucius-03-06.translation: The Ji family was to sacrifice on Mount Tai. The Master said to Ran You: can you not stop them? He said: I cannot. The Master said: ah — do they suppose Mount Tai knows less than Lin Fang?
confucius-03-06.note: A sacrifice out of rank will not be accepted. He reaches back to Lin Fang, who had just asked what ritual rests on.

confucius-03-07.translation: A person of character has nothing to contend over — unless it is archery. They bow and yield going up, come down, and drink together. Even their contending is becoming.
confucius-03-07.note: He does not remove the contest. He changes how it is carried out.

confucius-03-08a.translation: Zixia asked: a lovely smile dimpling, fine eyes clear, plain ground taken for the pattern — what does that mean? The Master said: the painting comes after the plain ground. Zixia said: then ritual comes after?
confucius-03-08a.note: From a remark about painting — ground first, pattern later — the student works out where ritual belongs.

confucius-03-08b.translation: It is Shang who lifts me. Now I can talk about the Odes with you.
confucius-03-08b.note: The one teaching is the one who gets woken up.

confucius-03-09.translation: I can speak of the rites of Xia, but Qi gives too little to confirm them; I can speak of the rites of Yin, but Song gives too little. The records are not enough. Were they enough, I could confirm it.
confucius-03-09.note: He keeps what can be said apart from what can be shown.

confucius-03-10.translation: At the di sacrifice, from the libation onward I would rather not watch.
confucius-03-10.note: He marks the point where the care at the start starts to slacken.

confucius-03-11.translation: Someone asked what the di sacrifice means. The Master said: I do not know. For one who did know, the world would be like looking at this — and he pointed to his palm.
confucius-03-11.note: He says he does not know, then shows only what the view would be for someone who did.

confucius-03-12.translation: Sacrifice as if they were present; sacrifice to the spirits as if the spirits were present. The Master said: a sacrifice I did not take part in is one I did not make.
confucius-03-12.note: Some things cannot be done on your behalf.

confucius-03-13.translation: Wangsun Jia asked: better to court the kitchen god than the god of the inner room — what does that mean? The Master said: not so. Offend heaven and there is nowhere left to pray.
confucius-03-13.note: Invited to court whoever holds real power, he answers by naming the one party you cannot court.

confucius-03-14.translation: Zhou looked to the two dynasties before it, and how rich its forms are. I follow Zhou.
confucius-03-14.note: His reason for choosing is how carefully it studied what came before.

confucius-03-15.translation: Entering the great temple, the Master asked about everything. Someone said: who called this man from Zou a man who knows ritual? He enters the great temple and asks about everything. Hearing it, the Master said: that is ritual.
confucius-03-15.note: One side reads the asking as ignorance. He reads it as the thing itself.

confucius-03-16.translation: In archery, piercing the hide is not the point, because strength is not of one grade. That was the old way.
confucius-03-16.note: Not measuring everyone by the same yardstick is also a kind of fairness.

confucius-03-17.translation: Zigong wanted to do away with the sheep offered at the new-moon announcement. The Master said: Si, you care about the sheep; I care about the ritual.
confucius-03-17.note: Even when only the form is left, losing the form means losing the place to return to.

confucius-03-18.translation: Serve your ruler with full ritual and people take it for flattery.
confucius-03-18.note: There are times when doing it properly is the thing that gets misread.

confucius-03-19.translation: Duke Ding asked: how should a ruler employ ministers, and ministers serve a ruler? Confucius answered: the ruler employs them by ritual, the ministers serve by loyalty.
confucius-03-19.note: The duty is not loaded onto one side. Each gets its own.

confucius-03-20.translation: The Guanju is joyful without excess, grieved without injury.
confucius-03-20.note: He does not praise the absence of feeling, but feeling that stops short of overflowing.

confucius-03-21a.translation: Duke Ai asked Zai Wo about the altar of the soil.
confucius-03-21a.note: One short line, but it sets off the exchange that follows.

confucius-03-21b.translation: Zai Wo answered: the Xia used pine, the Yin cypress, the Zhou chestnut — to make the people tremble. Hearing it, the Master said: what is done is not discussed, what is finished is not argued against, what is past is not blamed.
confucius-03-21b.note: He does not scold the pun-driven reading. He answers with how to treat what cannot be taken back.

confucius-03-22a.translation: The Master said: Guan Zhong was a small vessel. Someone asked: was he frugal? He had three residences and never doubled up his officials — how was he frugal? Then did Guan Zhong know ritual?
confucius-03-22a.note: Great achievements, and he still asks separately about the size of the vessel.

confucius-03-22b.translation: He said: a ruler of a state sets up a screen wall, and Guan did too; a ruler sets up a stand for cups when two rulers meet, and Guan did too. If Guan knew ritual, who does not?
confucius-03-22b.note: Two examples stand in place of an answer.

confucius-03-23.translation: Speaking of music to the grand master of Lu, the Master said: music can be understood. At the opening it gathers; as it goes on it is pure, it is clear, it is unbroken. And so it is completed.
confucius-03-23.note: Completion is not one moment but the sum of the textures passed through.

confucius-03-24a.translation: The border officer of Yi asked to be received, saying: when a person of character comes here, I have never failed to see them. The followers let him in.
confucius-03-24a.note: Spoken by someone whose post was never to turn a visitor away.

confucius-03-24b.translation: Coming out he said: why do you worry about his losing office? The world has long been without the way, and heaven is about to make your master its wooden bell.
confucius-03-24b.note: Being unused gets read as being put to a different use.

confucius-03-25.translation: Of the Shao he said: it is wholly beautiful and wholly good. Of the Wu: wholly beautiful, but not wholly good.
confucius-03-25.note: Beauty and rightness are measured separately, and he allows that they can come apart.

confucius-03-26.translation: Above others and not generous, performing ritual without respect, at a funeral without grief — what am I to look at?
confucius-03-26.note: For each position, form and occasion, he names what has to be present, not absent.

confucius-04-01.translation: To live among the humane is good. If you choose where to settle and it is not among them, where is the sense in that?
confucius-04-01.note: People come to resemble the place they put themselves in.

confucius-04-02.translation: One without humaneness cannot stay long in hardship, nor long in ease. The humane rest in humaneness; the wise find their advantage in it.
confucius-04-02.note: What lets someone hold up in both want and plenty is the question here.

confucius-04-03.translation: Only the humane can rightly like a person, or dislike one.
confucius-04-03.note: Only from someone unbiased does liking or disliking amount to a judgement.

confucius-04-04.translation: Set your mind truly on humaneness and there is no wrongdoing.
confucius-04-04.note: Once the direction is fixed, certain things simply stop happening.

confucius-04-05a.translation: Wealth and rank are what people want, but if they did not come by the right road, do not stay in them. Poverty and low standing are what people hate, but even if they did not come by the right road, do not scramble out of them. If a person of character lets go of humaneness, what is left to make a name on?
confucius-04-05a.note: The same test is applied to what you take and to what you escape.

confucius-04-05b.translation: A person of character does not depart from humaneness for the space of a single meal. In haste, they are there; in a stumble, they are there.
confucius-04-05b.note: The test does not come when there is time. It comes when there is none.

confucius-04-06a.translation: I have not met one who loves humaneness, nor one who hates what is not humane. Love it and nothing ranks above it; hate what is not humane and that itself is humaneness, keeping what is not humane off your person. Can anyone spend even one day's strength on it?
confucius-04-06a.note: Loving it and hating its absence are two roads to the same place.

confucius-04-06b.translation: I have not seen anyone whose strength was not enough. There may be such a person; I have not seen one.
confucius-04-06b.note: He sets being unable apart from not doing it.

confucius-04-07.translation: People's faults run true to their kind. Look at the fault and you know the humaneness.
confucius-04-07.note: Sometimes how someone goes wrong shows more than what they get right.

confucius-04-08.translation: Hear the way in the morning and you could die that evening.
confucius-04-08.note: He measures its weight by setting it against a life.

confucius-04-09.translation: A scholar set on the way who is ashamed of poor clothes and poor food is not worth talking things over with.
confucius-04-09.note: Declaring a purpose and accepting what it costs are not the same act.

confucius-04-10.translation: Toward the world, a person of character is neither set on a thing nor set against it; they go alongside what is right.
confucius-04-10.note: With no side decided in advance, you can take the right one each time.

confucius-04-11.translation: A person of character keeps character in mind; a lesser one keeps land. A person of character keeps the law in mind; a lesser one keeps favours.
confucius-04-11.note: What someone carries around in their head is the dividing line.

confucius-04-12.translation: Act with an eye on profit and you collect resentment.
confucius-04-12.note: The moment gain is divided, someone gets less.

confucius-04-13.translation: If you can run a state with ritual and yielding, what difficulty is there? If you cannot, what has ritual to do with it?
confucius-04-13.note: Ritual here is not ceremony but a method of governing.

confucius-04-14.translation: Do not worry about having no position; worry about what you would stand on. Do not worry that no one knows you; work at becoming worth knowing.
confucius-04-14.note: The worry is moved from outside to inside.

confucius-04-15.translation: Shen, my way is strung on a single thread. Zengzi said: yes. When the Master left, the disciples asked: what did he mean? Zengzi said: the Master's way is loyalty and reciprocity, nothing more.
confucius-04-15.note: One man takes it in a single word and passes it on in two.

confucius-04-16.translation: A person of character takes things in terms of what is right; a lesser one in terms of what it pays.
confucius-04-16.note: Hearing the same words, each translates them into a different currency.

confucius-04-17.translation: Meet someone admirable and think of matching them; meet someone who falls short and look inward.
confucius-04-17.note: Watching others turns directly into working on yourself.

confucius-04-18.translation: In serving your parents, remonstrate gently. If your view is not taken, stay respectful and do not oppose them; take the trouble and do not resent it.
confucius-04-18.note: Objecting and defying are kept apart.

confucius-04-19.translation: While your parents live, do not travel far; and if you travel, let it be to a known place.
confucius-04-19.note: Not a prohibition but a condition attached.

confucius-04-20.translation: If for three years one does not turn from the father's way, that may be called filial.
confucius-04-20.note: The same line appears in Book 2. It is recorded twice.

confucius-04-21.translation: You cannot not know your parents' age. On one side it gladdens you, on the other it frightens you.
confucius-04-21.note: The same number raises two feelings at once.

confucius-04-22.translation: The ancients did not let words out easily, ashamed that their conduct might not catch up.
confucius-04-22.note: The reason for saying little is located in shame.

confucius-04-23.translation: Few go wrong by holding themselves in.
confucius-04-23.note: The cost of doing less turns out to be smaller than expected.

confucius-04-24.translation: A person of character wants to be slow in speech and quick in action.
confucius-04-24.note: Which side should be slow and which quick does not get swapped.

confucius-04-25.translation: Character is not left alone. There will be neighbours.
confucius-04-25.note: Being alone now is not the same as being alone in the end.

confucius-04-26.translation: Press your ruler too often and you draw disgrace; press a friend too often and you drift apart.
confucius-04-26.note: Even closeness needs a gap left in it.

confucius-05-01.translation: Of Gongye Chang he said: a man to give a daughter to. He was once in bonds, but the fault was not his. And he gave him his daughter.
confucius-05-01.note: He separates the record from the person, and then acts on what he saw.

confucius-05-02.translation: Of Nan Rong he said: when the state has the way he will not be cast aside, and when it does not he will escape punishment. And he gave him his elder brother's daughter.
confucius-05-02.note: The test is whether someone gets through both the good times and the bad.

confucius-05-03.translation: Of Zijian he said: what a man of character. If Lu had no such men, where would he have got it?
confucius-05-03.note: Praising one person, he counts in the place that raised him.

confucius-05-04.translation: Zigong asked: and what about me? The Master said: you are a vessel. What kind? A jewelled temple vessel.
confucius-05-04.note: He had said a person of character is not a vessel. So this praise carries its own ceiling.

confucius-05-05.translation: Someone said: Yong is humane but has no gift for talk. The Master said: what is a gift for talk good for? Fending people off with a ready mouth earns you dislike again and again. I do not know whether he is humane — but what is a gift for talk good for?
confucius-05-05.note: He refuses to accept the named shortcoming as a shortcoming.

confucius-05-06.translation: The Master wanted Qidiao Kai to take office. He answered: I cannot yet feel sure of this. The Master was pleased.
confucius-05-06.note: The refusal is what pleases him: the man knows how to say not yet.

confucius-05-07.translation: If the way will not be followed, I would take a raft onto the sea — and the one to come with me would be You. Zilu heard it and was delighted. The Master said: You outdoes me in loving courage, but there is nothing to draw on there.
confucius-05-07.note: Taken as praise and received with delight, it immediately gets one layer peeled off.

confucius-05-08a.translation: Meng Wubo asked: is Zilu humane? The Master said: I do not know. Asked again, he said: You could be put in charge of the levies of a state of a thousand chariots. Whether he is humane, I do not know. And what of Qiu?
confucius-05-08a.note: He answers the question of ability in detail and leaves humaneness unanswered every time.

confucius-05-08b.translation: Qiu could be made steward of a town of a thousand households or a house of a hundred chariots. Whether he is humane, I do not know. And what of Chi? Chi, with his sash on, could stand at court and speak with the guests.
confucius-05-08b.note: The same shape of answer for all three shows the standard is not moving.

confucius-05-08c.translation: Whether he is humane, I do not know.
confucius-05-08c.note: The third answer closes the same way. Usefulness and humaneness are different questions.

confucius-05-09.translation: The Master said to Zigong: who is better, you or Hui? He answered: how could I look as high as Hui? He hears one thing and knows ten; I hear one and know two. The Master said: you are not his equal. Neither you nor I are his equal.
confucius-05-09.note: He accepts the student's own measure, then puts himself on the same side of it.

confucius-05-10a.translation: Zai Yu slept in the daytime. The Master said: rotten wood cannot be carved, a wall of dung-earth cannot be plastered. What is there to reprove in Yu? And he said: at first I listened to what people said and trusted what they did.
confucius-05-10a.note: One person makes him change the method itself.

confucius-05-10b.translation: Now I listen to what people say and watch what they do. Yu is the one who changed that in me.
confucius-05-10b.note: He records who it was that made the change.

confucius-05-11.translation: I have not seen a man of firmness. Someone said: Shen Cheng. The Master said: Cheng has wants. How could he be firm?
confucius-05-11.note: Firmness is not treated as strength but as having nothing you are after.

confucius-05-12.translation: Zigong said: what I do not want others to do to me, I would not do to them. The Master said: Si, that is not yet within your reach.
confucius-05-12.note: The statement is right and he still says not yet. Knowing it and arriving there are different.

confucius-05-13.translation: Zigong said: the Master's writings and outward teaching we could hear; his words on human nature and the way of heaven we could not.
confucius-05-13.note: A student puts on record that there was a region the teacher left unspoken.

confucius-05-14.translation: When Zilu had heard something and had not yet acted on it, his one fear was hearing something more.
confucius-05-14.note: Learning that piles up is treated as debt.

confucius-05-15.translation: Zigong asked: why was Kong Wenzi called Wen? The Master said: quick, and fond of learning, and not ashamed to ask those below him. That is why.
confucius-05-15.note: Not being ashamed to ask downward is what earns the name.

confucius-05-16.translation: Of Zichan he said: he had four ways of a person of character — in carrying himself, respectful; in serving above, reverent; in nurturing the people, generous; in employing them, just.
confucius-05-16.note: Four directions counted separately: self, above, below, and the work.

confucius-05-17.translation: Yan Pingzhong was good at friendship: the longer it lasted, the more respect he showed.
confucius-05-17.note: Time usually erodes formality. Here it deepens it.

confucius-05-18.translation: Zang Wenzhong kept a great tortoise, with hills carved on the capitals and pondweed painted on the posts. How was that wisdom?
confucius-05-18.note: Ornament out of rank is offered as evidence against his wisdom.

confucius-05-19a.translation: Zizhang asked: Prime Minister Ziwen took the post three times with no look of delight, and left it three times with no look of resentment, and always briefed his successor on the business of his term. How is that? The Master said: loyal.
confucius-05-19a.note: He gives praise, but one notch below what the question was reaching for.

confucius-05-19b.translation: Was he humane? I do not know; how would that be humane? When Cui killed the ruler of Qi, Chen Wenzi abandoned ten teams of horses and left. Reaching another state he said: they are just like our own Cui.
confucius-05-19b.note: He leaves, and finds the same thing waiting.

confucius-05-19c.translation: He left, came to another state, said again: they are just like our own Cui, and left. How is that? The Master said: clean. Was he humane? I do not know; how would that be humane?
confucius-05-19c.note: For both men, humaneness is the one word he will not hand over.

confucius-05-20.translation: Ji Wenzi thought three times before acting. Hearing of it the Master said: twice is enough.

confucius-05-21.translation: Ning Wuzi was wise when the state had the way, and a fool when it did not. His wisdom can be matched; his foolishness cannot.
confucius-05-21.note: Choosing to look like a fool is the harder of the two.

confucius-05-22.translation: In Chen he said: let us go home, let us go home. The young of my district are ambitious and rough; the pattern is there, but they do not know how to cut it.
confucius-05-22.note: He judges that the material is there and that a hand is needed, in the same breath.

confucius-05-23.translation: Boyi and Shuqi did not dwell on old wrongs, and so resentment toward them was rare.
confucius-05-23.note: The reason there is little resentment is located in how they remembered, not in whom they met.

confucius-05-24.translation: Who called Weisheng Gao straight? Someone asked him for vinegar, and he got it from a neighbour and gave it over.
confucius-05-24.note: In an act that looks kind, he points to where straightness bent. Straight would have been to say he had none.

confucius-05-25.translation: Polished words, a managed face, excessive deference — Zuo Qiuming was ashamed of these, and so am I. Hiding resentment and befriending the person anyway — Zuo Qiuming was ashamed of it, and so am I.
confucius-05-25.note: He takes an earlier man's standard over unchanged and makes it his own.

confucius-05-26a.translation: Yan Yuan and Jilu were in attendance. The Master said: why not each say what you are after? Zilu said: to share carriage, horses and coats with my friends, and feel no grudge when they wear out. Yan Yuan said: to make nothing of what I do well, and not parade my efforts.
confucius-05-26a.note: One answers toward sharing, the other toward not showing.

confucius-05-26b.translation: Zilu said: we would like to hear yours. The Master said: that the old be at ease, that friends trust me, that the young be cherished.
confucius-05-26b.note: He answers not with what he wants to be but with how he wants others to end up.

confucius-05-27.translation: It is hopeless. I have not met anyone who could see their own fault and put themselves on trial inwardly.
confucius-05-27.note: Knowing the fault and holding yourself to account for it are different things.

confucius-05-28.translation: In a hamlet of ten houses there is sure to be someone as loyal and reliable as I am. There will not be someone as fond of learning.
confucius-05-28.note: What he claims for himself is not the gift but the appetite for learning.

confucius-06-01a.translation: Yong could be set facing south. Zhonggong then asked about Zisang Bozi.
confucius-06-01a.note: Facing south means taking the ruler's seat. He places a student there.

confucius-06-01b.translation: He said: acceptable — simple. Zhonggong said: to hold oneself in reverence and act simply before the people, is that not acceptable? But to hold oneself simply and act simply too, is that not too simple? The Master said: Yong is right.
confucius-06-01b.note: Simplicity splits depending on where it sits. He takes the student's distinction as it stands.

confucius-06-02.translation: Duke Ai asked: which of your students loves learning? Confucius answered: there was Yan Hui. He loved learning — he did not shift his anger onto others and did not repeat a fault. Sadly his life was short and he died. Now there is none; I have not heard of one who loves learning.
confucius-06-02.note: Loving learning gets explained by exactly two behaviours.

confucius-06-03a.translation: Zihua was sent to Qi, and Ran You asked for grain for his mother. The Master said: give her a fu. He asked for more: give her a yu. Ran You gave her five bing.
confucius-06-03a.note: What was allowed and what was handed over come far apart.

confucius-06-03b.translation: The Master said: when Chi went to Qi he rode sleek horses and wore light furs. I have heard that a person of character helps the pressed, not tops up the well-off. When Yuan Si was made steward, he was given nine hundred of grain and declined.
confucius-06-03b.note: The same giving is judged by the state of the one receiving.

confucius-06-03c.translation: Do not refuse. Give it to the people of your lanes and villages.
confucius-06-03c.note: To the one refusing, he supplies a use for it.

confucius-06-04.translation: To Zhonggong he said: the calf of a plough ox, if it is red-haired and straight-horned — though they would not use it, would the hills and rivers pass it over?
confucius-06-04.note: Birth may be used to hold someone back, but the quality still gets noticed.

confucius-06-05.translation: Hui's heart did not depart from humaneness for three months. The rest reach it for a day or a month, and that is all.
confucius-06-05.note: The difference is measured not in depth but in how long it is held.

confucius-06-06a.translation: Ji Kangzi asked: could Zhong You be given charge of government? The Master said: You is decisive — what difficulty would government be? And Si? Si gets through to things — what difficulty would government be?
confucius-06-06a.note: A different single strength for each man, arriving at the same conclusion.

confucius-06-06b.translation: And Qiu? Qiu is accomplished — what difficulty would government be?
confucius-06-06b.note: The third answer keeps the same shape, so the standard stays put.

confucius-06-07.translation: The Ji family wanted Min Ziqian as steward of Bi. Min Ziqian said: make my excuses well. If anyone comes for me again, I will be up on the Wen.
confucius-06-07.note: He does not merely decline. He names where he will have gone.

confucius-06-08.translation: When Boniu fell ill the Master went to ask after him, took his hand through the window and said: we are losing him — it must be fate. That such a man should have such an illness. That such a man should have such an illness.
confucius-06-08.note: He does not explain. He says the same words twice.

confucius-06-09.translation: How fine Hui is. One bamboo bowl of rice, one gourd of water, a shabby lane — others could not bear the misery of it, and Hui does not let it change his joy. How fine Hui is.
confucius-06-09.note: Poverty is not the source of the joy. The joy simply stands apart from it.

confucius-06-10.translation: Ran Qiu said: it is not that I do not delight in your way; my strength is not enough. The Master said: those whose strength runs out give up halfway. You are drawing a line.
confucius-06-10.note: Stopping after trying and drawing a line before starting are kept apart.

confucius-06-11.translation: To Zixia he said: be the scholar of a person of character, not the scholar of a lesser one.
confucius-06-11.note: Even inside one calling, he sees a fork.

confucius-06-12.translation: Ziyou was steward of Wucheng. The Master asked: have you found anyone? He said: there is Tantai Mieming. He does not take shortcuts, and unless it is official business he has never come to my room.
confucius-06-12.note: A person is vouched for by two habits rather than by any achievement.

confucius-06-13.translation: Meng Zhifan did not boast. In the rout he covered the rear, and as he came to the gate he whipped his horse and said: it was not that I dared stay behind — the horse would not go.
confucius-06-13.note: He took the most dangerous place and handed the credit to his horse.

confucius-06-14.translation: Without Zhu Tuo's gift for talk, and with only Song Chao's good looks, it is hard to get through the present age.
confucius-06-14.note: A remark about the times, and about what the times reward.

confucius-06-15.translation: Who can go out except through the door? Then why does no one go by this way?
confucius-06-15.note: He sets it against something obvious, and asks why the obvious is not followed.

confucius-06-16.translation: Substance over polish and you are coarse; polish over substance and you are a clerk. When the two go together, then a person of character.
confucius-06-16.note: Not a choice between the two but a question of proportion.

confucius-06-17.translation: A person lives by being straight. To live crooked is to have got off by luck.
confucius-06-17.note: Getting away with it is not counted as being fine.

confucius-06-18.translation: Knowing it falls short of liking it; liking it falls short of delighting in it.
confucius-06-18.note: There are grades in how one comes at the same work.

confucius-06-19.translation: To those above the middle you can speak of what is above; to those below the middle you cannot.
confucius-06-19.note: Teaching is pitched to the listener, stated as a plain rule.

confucius-06-20.translation: Fan Chi asked about wisdom. The Master said: work at what is right for people, and respect the spirits while keeping your distance — that may be called wisdom. He asked about humaneness: the humane put the hard part first and the gain after; that may be called humaneness.
confucius-06-20.note: Wisdom is answered with distance, humaneness with order.

confucius-06-21.translation: The wise take to water, the humane take to mountains. The wise move, the humane are still. The wise are glad, the humane endure.
confucius-06-21.note: The two are set side by side as different grains, not ranked.

confucius-06-22.translation: Let Qi change once and it reaches Lu; let Lu change once and it reaches the way.
confucius-06-22.note: Not one leap but a step at a time.

confucius-06-23.translation: A cornered cup without corners — is that a cornered cup? Is that a cornered cup?
confucius-06-23.note: A single vessel stands for everything whose name and reality have come apart.

confucius-06-24.translation: Zai Wo asked: if the humane were told a man had fallen in a well, would they go in after him? The Master said: why would they? A person of character can be sent, but not trapped; can be deceived, but not blinded.
confucius-06-24.note: He turns back a question that would reduce humaneness to indiscriminate goodwill.

confucius-06-25.translation: A person of character learns widely in the texts and reins it in with ritual. Then they will not go astray.
confucius-06-25.note: Widening and binding are kept as a pair.

confucius-06-26.translation: The Master saw Nanzi, and Zilu was displeased. The Master swore: if there was anything unworthy in me, let heaven cast me off, let heaven cast me off.
confucius-06-26.note: No explanation, only an oath. The student's displeasure is written down as it was.

confucius-06-27.translation: The middle way as a virtue — how perfect it is. And how long it has been rare among people.
confucius-06-27.note: He calls it the highest and, in the same breath, the scarcest.

confucius-06-28a.translation: Zigong said: one who gave widely to the people and could rescue the many — how would that be? Could it be called humane? The Master said: why stop at humane? That would be a sage. Even Yao and Shun found it hard.
confucius-06-28a.note: The bar offered is too high to serve as the definition, so he sends it back.

confucius-06-28b.translation: The humane, wanting to stand, help others stand; wanting to arrive, help others arrive. To take the comparison from what is near at hand — that may be called the method of humaneness.
confucius-06-28b.note: In place of a grand achievement he offers a method: measure from your own case.

confucius-07-01.translation: I transmit, I do not invent; I trust the old and love it. Quietly I compare myself to Old Peng.
confucius-07-01.note: He defines his own work by what he does not do: make things up.

confucius-07-02.translation: To keep it in silence, to learn without tiring, to teach others without flagging — what else is there in me?
confucius-07-02.note: He names three things and says there is nothing else.

confucius-07-03.translation: Character left uncultivated, learning left unrehearsed, hearing what is right and not moving to it, faults not corrected — these are my worries.
confucius-07-03.note: Every item on the list is inside him, none outside.

confucius-07-04.translation: At leisure the Master was relaxed and easy, bright and at ease.
confucius-07-04.note: Not a teaching but a note on how he was when nothing was happening.

confucius-07-05.translation: How far I have declined. How long it has been since I dreamed of the Duke of Zhou.
confucius-07-05.note: He measures his decline by a dream that stopped coming.

confucius-07-06.translation: Set your mind on the way, hold to character, lean on humaneness, move freely among the arts.
confucius-07-06.note: Four verbs of decreasing grip, from setting the mind to moving freely. This edition writes xia for ju; the common reading is followed here.

confucius-07-07.translation: From a bundle of dried meat upward, I have never refused to teach anyone.
confucius-07-07.note: The threshold is set as low as it can go.

confucius-07-08.translation: I do not open it up for one who is not straining, nor draw it out of one who is not struggling for words. Show one corner, and if they do not come back with the other three, I do not repeat it.
confucius-07-08.note: The condition is set on the learner's readiness, not the teacher's.

confucius-07-09.translation: Eating beside one in mourning, the Master never ate his fill. On a day he had wailed, he did not sing.
confucius-07-09.note: Grief is not declared. It is kept in how the day is spent.

confucius-07-10a.translation: To Yan Yuan he said: used, then act; set aside, then withdraw. Only you and I have this. Zilu said: if you led three armies, whom would you take?
confucius-07-10a.note: Praise meant for two, and Zilu cuts in. The way he asks shows who he is.

confucius-07-10b.translation: One who would take on a tiger bare-handed or cross a river on foot, and die with no regret — I would not take him. It would have to be one who approaches a task with fear, and likes to plan it through.
confucius-07-10b.note: Courage is placed on the side that knows fear, not the side that lacks it.

confucius-07-11.translation: If wealth could be had by seeking, I would take even the whip-holder's post. Since it cannot, I follow what I love.
confucius-07-11.note: He does not scorn wealth. He judges that seeking does not produce it.

confucius-07-12.translation: What the Master treated with care: fasting, war, illness.
confucius-07-12.note: Three areas he handled carefully. Each of them touches life itself.

confucius-07-13.translation: In Qi he heard the Shao, and for three months did not notice the taste of meat. He said: I never imagined music could reach this far.
confucius-07-13.note: The impression is recorded not as an exclamation but as a length of time.

confucius-07-14a.translation: Ran You said: is the Master for the ruler of Wei? Zigong said: very well, I will ask him.
confucius-07-14a.note: He decides not to ask directly. The next passage is the method.

confucius-07-14b.translation: He went in and asked: what sort of men were Boyi and Shuqi? Worthy men of old. Did they feel resentment? They sought humaneness and got it; what was there to resent? He came out and said: the Master is not for him.
confucius-07-14b.note: He asks about two brothers who gave up a throne, and so gets an answer about a quarrel over one.

confucius-07-15.translation: Coarse rice to eat, water to drink, a bent arm for a pillow — there is joy in the middle of that too. Wealth and rank got unjustly are to me like drifting clouds.
confucius-07-15.note: He shows where the joy is before naming where it is not.

confucius-07-16.translation: Give me a few more years, and let me study the Changes at fifty, and I could be free of great faults.
confucius-07-16.note: He says there is still more to learn, and puts an age on it.

confucius-07-17.translation: The Master used the correct pronunciation for the Odes, the Documents, and the conduct of ritual — all in the correct speech.
confucius-07-17.note: A note that in formal settings he read in the standard pronunciation.

confucius-07-18.translation: The Duke of She asked Zilu about Confucius, and Zilu did not answer. The Master said: why did you not say — he is the sort who forgets to eat when he is fired up, forgets his cares in his joy, and does not notice old age coming on.
confucius-07-18.note: He writes his own introduction and hands it over.

confucius-07-19.translation: I was not born knowing. I love the old and go after it diligently.
confucius-07-19.note: He denies the gift and explains himself by the pursuit.

confucius-07-20.translation: The Master did not talk of: the uncanny, feats of strength, disorder, spirits.
confucius-07-20.note: A list of what he left unsaid, which shows where his attention went.

confucius-07-21.translation: Walking with two others, I am sure to have a teacher among them. I pick out what is good and follow it, and what is not good I correct in myself.
confucius-07-21.note: Both the good and the bad are made to yield something.

confucius-07-22.translation: Heaven gave me this character. What can Huan Tui do to me?
confucius-07-22.note: Said with his life under threat.

confucius-07-23.translation: Do you suppose I hold something back? I hold nothing back. There is nothing I do that I do not do with you — that is who I am.
confucius-07-23.note: The teaching is offered not as words but as all the time spent together.

confucius-07-24.translation: The Master taught four things: the texts, conduct, loyalty, reliability.
confucius-07-24.note: Knowledge, action and character bundled into one curriculum.

confucius-07-25a.translation: A sage I shall not get to see; if I could see a person of character, that would do. A good man I shall not get to see; if I could see one with constancy, that would do.

confucius-07-25b.translation: Nothing, and acting as if something; empty, and acting as if full; pinched, and acting as if comfortable — constancy is hard.
confucius-07-25b.note: The scarcity of constancy is traced to the habit of pretending.

confucius-07-26.translation: The Master fished with a line but not with a net, and shot with a corded arrow but never at a roosting bird.
confucius-07-26.note: Not abstaining, but drawing a line inside the act.

confucius-07-27.translation: There may be those who make things up without knowing; I am not one. Hear much, pick out the good and follow it; see much and keep it in mind. That is the next best thing to knowing.
confucius-07-27.note: He grades his own knowledge and puts it second.

confucius-07-28.translation: The people of Huxiang were hard to talk with. A boy from there was received, and the disciples were puzzled. The Master said: I accept their coming forward, not their going back. Why be so harsh? If someone cleans himself up and comes forward, I accept the cleaning. I do not hold his past as security.
confucius-07-28.note: The past is not made a condition. Only the step forward is counted.

confucius-07-29.translation: Is humaneness far off? I want it, and it is here.
confucius-07-29.note: A question of distance is turned into a question of wanting.

confucius-07-30a.translation: The minister of justice of Chen asked: did Duke Zhao know ritual? Confucius answered: he knew ritual. When Confucius had withdrawn, the minister bowed Wuma Qi forward and said: I have heard that a person of character takes no sides. Do they take sides after all?
confucius-07-30a.note: An answer that shielded his own ruler comes straight back as a charge.

confucius-07-30b.translation: The ruler took a wife from Wu of the same surname and called her Wu Mengzi. If he knew ritual, who does not? Wuma Qi reported it, and the Master said: I am fortunate — if I have a fault, people are sure to know it.
confucius-07-30b.note: He does not argue back. He takes being caught as luck.

confucius-07-31.translation: When the Master sang with someone and it was good, he always had them sing it again, and then joined in.
confucius-07-31.note: Meeting something good, the first move is to hear it again.

confucius-07-32.translation: In letters I am probably no worse than others; in carrying out the person of character in my own conduct, I have got nowhere yet.
confucius-07-32.note: He splits knowing from doing and puts himself on the second side.

confucius-07-33.translation: Sage and humane — how could I presume? But that I work at it without tiring and teach others without flagging, that much may be said. Gongxi Hua said: that is exactly what we cannot learn.
confucius-07-33.note: What he sets down as modesty, a student picks back up.

confucius-07-34.translation: The Master was gravely ill and Zilu asked to pray. Is there such a thing? There is; the prayer text says, we pray for you to the spirits above and below. The Master said: my praying has gone on a long time.
confucius-07-34.note: He neither refuses the prayer nor accepts it, but moves it to another sense.

confucius-07-35.translation: Extravagance makes you immodest, frugality makes you stiff. Rather stiff than immodest.
confucius-07-35.note: Both are faults; he picks the lesser one.

confucius-07-36.translation: A person of character is level and broad; a lesser one is forever fretting.
confucius-07-36.note: How the inside shows on the outside.

confucius-07-37.translation: The Master was warm yet stern, commanding yet not fierce, respectful yet at ease.
confucius-07-37.note: Three pairs that do not usually combine, offered as a portrait.

confucius-08-01.translation: Taibo may be called the highest character. Three times he yielded the realm, and left the people nothing to praise him for.
confucius-08-01.note: Yielding without leaving a trace is counted as part of it.

confucius-08-02.translation: Respectful without ritual is wearing; careful without ritual is timid; brave without ritual is disorderly; straight without ritual is harsh. If those above are devoted to their kin, the people rise toward humaneness; if old ties are not dropped, the people do not turn mean.
confucius-08-02.note: Four good qualities, all of them listing over without ritual to hold them.

confucius-08-03.translation: Zengzi fell ill and called his students: uncover my feet, uncover my hands. The Odes say, in fear and trembling, as at the edge of a deep gorge, as treading thin ice. From now on I know I am free of it, my boys.
confucius-08-03.note: A man careful all his life says only at the end that it is over.

confucius-08-04a.translation: Zengzi was ill and Meng Jingzi came to ask after him. Zengzi said: when a bird is dying its cry is sad; when a man is dying his words are good. In the way there are three things a person of character prizes. In bearing and movement, keep violence and sloth far off.
confucius-08-04a.note: He frames it as last words first, then names the three.

confucius-08-04b.translation: Set your face right and you come near to being trusted; in speech and tone, keep the coarse and perverse far off. As for the ritual vessels, there are officers for that.
confucius-08-04b.note: He separates what is his to mind from what belongs to someone else.

confucius-08-05.translation: Able, and asking those who are not; having much, and asking those with little; having, as if not; full, as if empty; wronged, and not keeping score. Long ago a friend of mine managed this.
confucius-08-05.note: He does not name him, only calls him a friend.

confucius-08-06.translation: One you could entrust an orphaned heir to, to whom you could commit the fate of a hundred li, who at the great crisis cannot be turned. Is such a one a person of character? He is.
confucius-08-06.note: Three conditions, then he puts the question and answers it himself.

confucius-08-07.translation: A scholar cannot but be broad and firm: the load is heavy and the road long. He takes humaneness as his load — is it not heavy? He stops only at death — is it not long?
confucius-08-07.note: A whole life measured in weight and distance.

confucius-08-08.translation: Roused by the Odes, set on your feet by ritual, completed by music.
confucius-08-08.note: The course of learning compressed into three stages.

confucius-08-09.translation: The people can be made to follow it; they cannot be made to know it.
confucius-08-09.note: A long-argued line. Punctuated differently it reads either as must not be told or as cannot easily be told.

confucius-08-10.translation: To love courage and hate poverty brings disorder. To hate the inhumane too fiercely also brings disorder.
confucius-08-10.note: He points to two opposite places where trouble starts.

confucius-08-11.translation: Even with the gifts and grace of the Duke of Zhou, if a man is arrogant and grudging, the rest is not worth looking at.
confucius-08-11.note: Two faults outweigh the whole sum of the talent.

confucius-08-12.translation: Three years of study without the mind turning to a salary — that is not easily found.
confucius-08-12.note: He marks the point where learning tilts toward a living.

confucius-08-13a.translation: Hold fast in trust and love learning; guard it to the death and keep the way good. Do not enter a state in danger, do not live in one in disorder. When the world has the way, appear; when it does not, hide. If the state has the way and you are poor and low, that is a shame.
confucius-08-13a.note: Whether to step forward or back is decided by the state of things outside.

confucius-08-13b.translation: If the state is without the way and you are rich and exalted, that is a shame.
confucius-08-13b.note: Paired with the line before it, the same test applied from the other side.

confucius-08-14.translation: If you are not in the post, do not plan its business.
confucius-08-14.note: The boundary of involvement is drawn at the office held.

confucius-08-15.translation: The opening by the music master Zhi, and the finale of the Guanju — how it surges and fills the ear.
confucius-08-15.note: A memory of music set down as sensation.

confucius-08-16.translation: Ambitious but not straight, simple but not sincere, artless but not reliable — such people I do not understand.
confucius-08-16.note: A flaw usually brings its own compensating virtue. Here even that is missing.

confucius-08-17.translation: Learn as if you could not catch up, and still fear losing it.
confucius-08-17.note: The strain of catching up and the fear of losing it, laid on top of each other.

confucius-08-18.translation: How lofty: Shun and Yu held the realm, and took no part in it for themselves.
confucius-08-18.note: Holding something and being bound up in it are kept apart.

confucius-08-19.translation: How great Yao was as a ruler. How lofty — only heaven is great, and only Yao took it for his model. How vast: the people could find no name for it. How lofty his achievement, how brilliant his forms.
confucius-08-19.note: That no name could be found is used as the highest praise.

confucius-08-20a.translation: Shun had five ministers and the realm was governed. King Wu said: I have ten who bring order. Confucius said: talent is hard to find — is it not so? The age of Tang and Yu was the richest in it, and one of them was a woman, so there were nine.
confucius-08-20a.note: He counts the figures out and so proves the scarcity.

confucius-08-20b.translation: Holding two parts of the realm in three and still serving Yin — the character of Zhou may be called the highest.
confucius-08-20b.note: Having the power and not using it is what gets counted.

confucius-08-21.translation: In Yu I find nothing to fault. Plain in food and drink, yet full of devotion in sacrifice; coarse in clothing, yet splendid in ceremonial robes; humble in his house, yet pouring his strength into the channels and ditches. In Yu I find nothing to fault.
confucius-08-21.note: What he spent on himself against what he spent on the public work, in three pairs.

confucius-09-01.translation: The Master seldom spoke of profit, of fate, or of humaneness.
confucius-09-01.note: A note that he rarely raised what mattered most, long discussed because of it.

confucius-09-02.translation: A man of Daxiang said: how great Confucius is — widely learned, and famous for nothing in particular. Hearing it, the Master said to his students: what shall I take up? Charioteering? Archery? I shall take up charioteering.
confucius-09-02.note: Told he has no specialty, he takes it as a joke and plays along.

confucius-09-03.translation: A hemp cap is the rite; now silk is used, which is thriftier, and I go with the many. Bowing below the hall is the rite; now they bow above, which is presumptuous. Though it sets me against the many, I bow below.
confucius-09-03.note: In one passage, both when to follow custom and when to break it.

confucius-09-04.translation: The Master was free of four things: no guessing, no insisting, no rigidity, no self.
confucius-09-04.note: The portrait is made of four absences rather than four virtues.

confucius-09-05.translation: In danger at Kuang he said: King Wen is gone — is his culture not here? If heaven meant to destroy it, one born later could not have had a share in it. Since heaven has not destroyed it, what can the men of Kuang do to me?
confucius-09-05.note: He reads the situation not by his own safety but by whether what he carries survives.

confucius-09-06a.translation: The grand steward asked Zigong: is your master a sage? How is he so capable in so many things? Zigong said: heaven surely set him free to be a sage, and he is capable besides. Hearing it the Master said: the grand steward knows me.
confucius-09-06a.note: He passes over the student's elevation and praises the questioner instead.

confucius-09-06b.translation: I was poor when young, so I am good at humble tasks. Is a person of character good at many things? Not many.
confucius-09-06b.note: He traces the skills to poverty and declines the word sage.

confucius-09-07.translation: Lao said: the Master said, I was not employed, and so I have skills.
confucius-09-07.note: It follows the passage before. The time of not being used is what made the skills.

confucius-09-08.translation: Do I have knowledge? I do not. When a plain man asks me something, I feel quite empty; I knock at both ends of it and draw it all out.
confucius-09-08.note: Knowledge is explained not as a store but as a way of drawing things out.

confucius-09-09.translation: The phoenix does not come, the river yields no chart. I am finished.
confucius-09-09.note: He reads the prospects for his own work in the signs of the age.

confucius-09-10.translation: Seeing someone in mourning, someone in ceremonial dress, or someone blind, the Master always rose, even if they were young, and quickened his step in passing.
confucius-09-10.note: Whom to honour is settled by circumstance, not by rank.

confucius-09-11a.translation: Yan Yuan sighed and said: look up and it is higher; bore into it and it is harder; see it ahead, and suddenly it is behind. The Master leads people on step by step: he broadened me with the texts and reined me in with ritual.
confucius-09-11a.note: A rare record of the teacher as the student saw him.

confucius-09-11b.translation: I cannot stop even if I want to; I have spent all I have. Something stands there towering, and though I want to follow it, there is no road.
confucius-09-11b.note: The closer he gets, the clearer the distance becomes.

confucius-09-12a.translation: The Master was gravely ill, and Zilu had the disciples pose as retainers. When the illness eased he said: how long You has been at this deceit. To have no retainers and pretend to have them — whom would I deceive? Would I deceive heaven?
confucius-09-12a.note: Done out of kindness, a pretence is still a pretence.

confucius-09-12b.translation: And rather than die in the hands of retainers, would I not sooner die in yours? And even without a grand funeral, am I going to die by the roadside?
confucius-09-12b.note: Refusing the formalities, he puts his students above them.

confucius-09-13.translation: Zigong said: if there were a fine jade here, would you box it up and hide it, or look for a good price and sell? The Master said: sell it, sell it. I am one who waits for the price.
confucius-09-13.note: He makes clear he is not hiding but waiting.

confucius-09-14.translation: The Master wanted to live among the nine tribes. Someone said: they are crude; how could you? The Master said: if a person of character lives there, what crudeness would there be?
confucius-09-14.note: A question about the place is moved to the person living in it.
